value: Poole admits Utterson to Jekyll’s cabinet. Utterson asks if Jekyll has heard the news; Jekyll swears he will never see Hyde again. Jekyll gives Utterson a letter signed Edward Hyde, saying he burned the envelope, which had no postmark, and that Hyde dictated his will. Poole says no letter came except by post. Hearing newsboys cry an M.P.’s murder, Utterson shows Guest the murderer’s letter. Guest finds it identical to Jekyll’s note. Utterson locks it in his safe, suspecting forgery.
